liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Ollin Arageed instrumental** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds Hamza El Din's piece wonderful and thinks the surrounding jamming is interesting and worth hearing; Reviewer describes Ollin as repetitive, rolling and melodic, with Jerry's guitar weaving in and out [8][11]
- **Jam # 1** (1 review): Reviewer hears Jam 1 opening with a Hamza El Din jam [7]
- **Ollin Arrageed** (1 review): Reviewer enjoys the Hamza jams but is less taken with the Ollin Arageed piece [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Jam # 1**: back after 246 archived shows (1758 days); rare: 4 archived performances [12]
- **Jam #2**: back after 246 archived shows (1758 days); rare: 5 archived performances [12]
- **Jam # 3**: back after 432 archived shows (2580 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [12]
- **Jam # 4**: back after 432 archived shows (2580 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [12]
- **Jam # 5**: back after 432 archived shows (2580 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [12]
- **Jam # 6**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [12]
- **Jam # 7**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [12]
- **Jam # 8**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [12]

## The recordings

- **gd78-09-13.sndchk-sbd.wiley.11482.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 33 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this circulating copy is an audience recording, not a soundboard as labeled [6]
- **gd78-09-13.sndchk-aud.jim.10155.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 4 songs; 33 min [2]. Said about its sound: Wind sometimes intrudes on the microphones, but it often adds to the ambience [2]
- **gd1978-09-13.136808.sndck.FOB.schall.flac16**: audience recording; 1 songs; 9 min [4]. Said about its sound: Microphones were mostly hidden behind a cotton headpiece, so levels can sound muffled; this is not a transfer artifact [4]
- **gd1978-09-13.136808.FOB.sndck.schall.flac16**: audience recording; 1 songs; 9 min [5]. Said about its sound: Microphones were mostly hidden behind a cotton headpiece, so levels can sound muffled; this is not a transfer artifact [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer places the Ollin performance at the Sphinx, in warm desert air [11]
- The singer and string player may be Hamza el-Din; the Dead seem present only on the first song [2]
- The tape contains the entire Hamza opener [4]
- The tape contains the entire Hamza opener [5]
- The same Hamza El Din theme is heard before Shakedown on 11/23/78, according to the reviewer [7]
- Reviewer says the Giza shows were far from the band's best [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd78-09-13.sndchk-sbd.wiley.11482.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd78-09-13.sndchk-aud.jim.10155.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [2]. Also: Audience cassette master, then an unknown step, then CD; provided by Jim Bennett [2]
- **gd1978-09-13.136808.sndck.FOB.schall.flac16**: transferred by John D'Auria; Dave Schall; source: Source: Aud FOB, front row LFC, Sony ECM280 > Sony TC-153 cassette recorder; [4]. Also: Taped in 1978 by "The Face" on reel to reel; transferred using an Apogee [4]
- **gd1978-09-13.136808.FOB.sndck.schall.flac16**: source: Source: Aud FOB, front row LFC, Sony ECM280 > Sony TC-153 cassette recorder; [5]. Also: Taped in 1978 by "The Face" on reel to reel; transferred by John with an Apogee [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Poster - Giza Sound and Light Theater](https://www.dead.net/archives/1978/artwork/poster-giza-sound-and-light-theater) [13]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [current-page:url:arg:3 | Grateful Dead](https://www.dead.net/tags/giza) [14]
